newsitem.title: UK: Signs of damage appear on dry east England grains.
newsitem.headline: Signs of damage appear on dry east England grains.

text.p: Signs have emerged that a lack of rain in eastern England may be causing real damage to the developing grains crop, farming industry sources said.
"Crops are starting to yellow, especially the late drilled ones," one co-op manager in the area said. "With no prospect of rain, people are getting concerned."
"People are beginning to say the lack of rain is having a real effect," a farm industry analyst added. "We need substantial rain in the next two or three weeks."
Until recently British agriculturalists have said the crops looked good, despite concerns over the lack of moisture.
Farmers in East Anglia were talking about a reduction of up to 20 per cent in yield, the analyst said. But they were by far the worst affected.
Conditions in Scotland, which has missed the dry spell, had been good, he said.

Although there have been showers, and more are forecast, there is no real sign of significant rain for much of England in the next five days, "especially for the eastern side of the country," a spokesman for the Meteorological Office said.
In the longer term, the office was sticking to its forecast of possible rain in the first half of May, although the spokesman stressed the limitations of long term weather forecasts.
